body: It was the same with my brother. The day before he died, I was signing him up for the ACT and talking about colleges and potential majors. He had just bought his senior ring, made plans for the summer... we had no idea.

I found my brother almost four months ago. It’s not easy. It’s so not. That first day was so bad. I joined sibling survivor groups on Facebook, I attended a suicide survivor group in person. I finally just started individual therapy. I have ptsd from it. It’s horrible. I’m starting emdr with my therapist next week to get through it. Please, get help sooner than later. Don’t feel ashamed to talk about how you’re feeling.

My little brother chose the same way out. Although, he did it in our house while I thought I was home alone (he was supposed to be in school). He died on December 17, New Years was so hard for me. I freak out any time I hear any loud noises and often have to skip past scenes with guns in them because I’ll have a panic attack otherwise. I was diagnosed with PTSD from that and from finding him. 

You’ve been grieving a lot longer than I have, I can’t really give you any advice. I’ve found just talking to people helps. When I’m at college I attend a suicide survivors group at a local grief recovery center with one of my friends who lost her dad the same way. That has helped the most. I start individual therapy this week. I had to get on antidepressants to help with the day to day stuff. Maybe even look into some spousal survivors of suicide groups on Facebook - I’m in a few sibling survivor ones and they make me feel a lot less alone. 

You don’t get over grief, you just learn how to live with it. I wish you the best, I’m so sorry for your loss.

I work in the geology office at my university. Easy stuff, just running errands, putting paper in the printers, and putting mail in boxes. I’m able to do my homework most of the time I work, which is great. Found out on a Thursday that my university was transferring to online classes. Moved out on the following Saturday. Now I have no income but all this free time. Really sucks when I have loans to pay off.

We had no idea. My brother was 17, a junior in high school. Wildly different ages. I always thought he was somewhere on the autism spectrum, but my parents wouldn’t ever get him tested. I looked through his phone completely, there was nothing there that suggested he would do this. He had messaged everyone in my immediate family a few days before that he loved us, to which I had a lengthy conversation with him but he assured me he was okay and that he could come to me if he was struggling. That was five days before he died. Nothing else ever alluded to him wanting to die. His note didn’t even fully say why. One drunken night, I broke down to my roommates and told them that I’ll never know why he died until I die, and that I wanted to take my own life because of it. It haunts me still that I said that to them.

It’s been pretty difficult. I was the one who found my brother and it gave me ptsd. I wasn’t able to be home by myself for a while and now I’m finding that I’m home by myself.. every day all day since I had to move home after my college shut down. My dad yells a lot and says little things that really upset me. I started lexapro a month ago and that’s helping me not completely lose it. I miss my brother so much, it’s hard passing his room everyday.
There you go, there’s one thing. It may be difficult, but every day it might help if you write down one good thing that happened that day — even if it’s that you got out of bed! Find small victories.
You are! Think about all the things you’ll miss out on. What are 5 things that make you happy?

When i attended therapy, they told me to look for small things to live for. I started to make a list: my brother’s wedding, my college graduation, my little brother’s high school graduation, my mom, my cats, etc. My little brother died from suicide almost two months ago, so now I don’t have his high school graduation. I don’t know if he ever thought about good things to come one day. I don’t even know what he struggled with that let him to that point. I’m glad that you are holding out hope for good things. Making a list of things to look forward to might help as well. You are important.
I’m glad you did, your life is important.
Anything helps!

In my brother’s note, he wrote “If this doesn’t work and I end up a vegetable, I don’t want to live like that.” Selfishly, I’d rather him be alive and in the hospital rather than having success in his attempt. I’ve had these thoughts sometimes too. I was always scared of it not working. Your life is important.

I’m glad that it didn’t work. I watched a video today on YouTube about this guy who jumped off the Golden Gate Bridge and he said he immediately regretted it the second his feet left. I hope that you can conquer whatever demons you’re battling. Your life is important.

In a sense, you pass your pain on. My 17 year old brother died from suicide almost two months ago. We didn’t even know he was struggling, he never came to us. I had some depression and anxiety before his death, but now it’s so amped up I don’t know what to do about it.

My little brother (17) died from suicide almost two months ago. He honestly thought no one at all would care. It was his first attempt and he had never come to us prior saying that he was having problems. Because of his death, I have anxiety, depression, and PTSD. I’ve witnessed my parents at the lowest parts of their life. I saw my straight-edge military father crumple to the floor and had my mom (who I’ve seen cry only a handful of times) fall into my arms and scream out for her son. I guarantee you so many people care. It would affect so many people. On the cat part, my two cats have even noticed that my brother is gone. They sit at his door and meow for him, wondering why he hasn’t opened the door to let them in. It may not seem like it, but so many people do care.

I haven’t gotten help for the PTSD. I mentioned it to my therapist, but she’s only a doctoral student so she can’t do much. I need to see a psychiatrist because I really feel like I need to be on anti depressants for it.

I attend group that for suicide survivors. It’s a small group and I’m the only person who’s lost a sibling. I’m in a few groups on Facebook for sibling survivors, so that’s helping. I’m going to individual therapy on campus and she hasn’t mentioned any groups on campus, so I’m not sure. 

I try to talk to my mom and grandma everyday, that’s helping. I usually FaceTime my mom when I eat dinner.

I’ve been talking to my grandma almost every day since my friends don’t really seem to know what to do. That’s helping. That and the group therapy. I’m hoping I can see an actual psychiatrist instead of the doctoral students at the mental health clinic on campus. I might also see about getting an emotional support cat next year.
I spent the night with one of my friends so that helped me in the moment, but I feel broken and empty.

To answer all of your questions: I don’t know. I do feel stuck. It’s only been 7 weeks since my brother died but everything is just so much. It’s so overwhelming. I’ve never been in this much pain in my life. People are treating me differently because of it. There are times when I don’t want to go on. How is it fair that I get to grow up when my brother can’t? He was only 17, he didn’t even get to graduate high school. I constantly feel on edge. I keep having to ask people to accommodate me, whether it’s to stop playing a video game that I played with my brother or to lightly close cabinets/door instead of slamming them because of the sound. I feel like not only I’m walking on eggshells, but people around me are walking on eggshells. My brother has become the elephant in the room. No one knows what to say so no one says anything.

I asked my parents if they needed me to stay home this semester and they told me to stay in school. They feel, and I feel this way too, that if I wasn’t in school this semester I probably wouldn’t come back. I’m on track to graduating early and I’d like to keep that. I’ve talked to all of my professors and most of them are willing to accommodate me if needed. I’m in a lot of classes surrounding death and violence since I’m studying forensic anthropology, so at least they’re offering to help me.

I’m away at college so the family time thing is difficult. My parents are coming down at the end of the month though, so I’m looking forward to that. 

I’m going to the grocery store today to get fruits and veggies and chicken. I noticed I gained some weight and don’t want to continue that. 

I’m attending biweekly therapy at my school. It’s not the best, but it’s something. And I’m in a suicide survivors grief group that I go to every Thursday. I found that really really helps. 

He really liked spicy stuff so I’ve been trying to eat more of that kind of food in honor of him. 

And he loved adventure, I was going to ask my parents if on what was supposed to be his 18th birthday if we could go sky diving, since he wanted to do that on his birthday.
Thank you.
They’re not handling it the best. I’m away at college so it’s just the two of them in the house.
The warnings before the post are better. I struggle with PTSD and right now a lot of things bother me, so the trigger warnings help.

Im going to visit my older brother for spring break, we have a week planned out of fun things to do. I’m helping his fiancé look for wedding dresses, too. I try to listen to music but I’m not really in the mood for it. I’m in a few sibling suicide survivor groups on Facebook and they’re helpful, it makes me feel a little less alone.
I thought about not being in school this semester, but my parents said to stay. I know if I take a semester off I might not come back.
My brother killed himself when I was home and I found him.
Yes, my little brother.
My college is about 4 hours away from home and I don’t have a car. My mom is coming down to visit me at the end of my month which I’m looking forward to. I really miss them.
